findings.reason: implemented as written the request is either restored `queued` (never reaching `launch-failed`) or written `launch-failed` with no `admit_request` and therefore never re-queued, so the section's own "on a later pass" claim fails and an invalid steering file strands the node.
findings.text: §5 says an invalid `steering.md` "moves the request to `launch-failed` with the failure named, as any launch failure does today, and `_requeue_admitted_failures` returns it to `queued` on a later pass"; but a steering check inside `_launch_queued` raises before `dispatch()` returns, so `admit_once` catches it and `_record_queued_failure` restores the pointer as `queued` with the failure and a `_retry_backoff_hold` (queue_admission.py:1957-1972, :804-833), while `launch-failed` is written only for a launched run whose process died before reaching a model (dispatch_launch.py:330, dispatch_sessions.py:314) — and `_requeue_admitted_failures` skips any pointer without `admit_request` (:760-761), which is stamped only after a successful launch (`_stamp_admission`, :2049)

findings.reason: §9 queues exactly these section-only requests, so as written the binding mechanism blocks the plan's own loading path until the repointing is made conditional on the file existing.
findings.text: §5 says `_launch_queued` "points the node's `brief` and `brief_path` at that file in place of the queue-time values `_node_from_pointer` carries" with no condition, but a request whose authority is a plan section alone ("a plan section, a steering file, or both") has no `steering.md`: `queue_dispatch` copies `--brief` only when the node carries one, and `plan_dispatch` takes `_brief_digest(node.brief_path or node.brief)` whenever `node.brief.strip()` is non-empty (dispatch_plan.py:830-834), so a repointed-but-absent path makes every section-only queued request fail its launch with "the brief ... is not readable"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol and path §5's changed text names resolves: `queue_dispatch` (runs.py:546), `_queued_request_record` (dispatch.py:229), `_launch_queued` (queue_admission.py:171), `_node_from_pointer` (queue_admission.py:119), `_requeue_admitted_failures` (queue_admission.py:748), `_store_brief` (dispatch_admission.py:2241), `_brief_digest` (dispatch_admission.py:2204), and all six declared write paths exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5 now declares a discriminating arm (leave `steering.md` alone, change the file the pointer's `node.brief` names, require the worker's digest to match `steering.md` and fail on today's code) plus an in-place re-queue arm and a refused-edit arm, so the measure can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log is stated under the request's own run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<request-id>/`), which is durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed text introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose; `launch-failed` and `steering.md` are runtime vocabulary, not plan identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — (a) the launch-failure arm names a phase and a re-queue function that the synchronous refusal path never produces, and (b) the launch repointing of `brief`/`brief_path` at `steering.md` is stated unconditionally, while a request whose authority is a plan section alone has no such file.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5's two-node split (binding, then verbs) is declared in its own done-when and was declined as one deliverable by an earlier review; the changed text does not reopen it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's declared edge `s5 -> a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan#s2` is the only dependency the changed text needs (the request-phase vocabulary, `awaiting-upstream`, and `launch-failed` all come from §2's landed implementation).
